definitions.gloss: looks interesting; looks like fun; sounds fun
definitions.explanation: An appearance-based judgement that something seems interesting or enjoyable, based on what the speaker has seen or heard about it. Formed from {面白|おもしろ}い + the evidential suffix そう.

examples.japanese: その{映画|えいが}は{面白|おもしろ}そうだ。
{面白|おもしろ}そうな{本|ほん}を{見|み}つけた。
{新|あたら}しい{仕事|しごと}の{内容|ないよう}を{聞|き}いて、とても{面白|おもしろ}そうだと{思|おも}った。
examples.english: After hearing what the new job involves, I thought it sounded really interesting.

notes:
Formed by attaching the evidential そう suffix to the stem of the i-adjective {面白|おもしろ}い (drop い, add そう). The result conjugates as a na-adjective: {面白|おもしろ}そうだ (predicate) / {面白|おもしろ}そうな (modifier) / {面白|おもしろ}そうに (adverbial).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {面白|おもしろ}そうな{話|はなし}: an interesting-sounding story
- {面白|おもしろ}そうに{聞|き}こえる: to sound interesting
- {面白|おもしろ}そうにしている: to look like one is having fun

USAGE:
Used only when the speaker has not yet experienced the thing directly. After actually trying it, switch to plain {面白|おもしろ}い. Saying *{面白|おもしろ}そうな{映画|えいが}だった about a movie you have already watched sounds odd.
